title: Optimal exact-distance label length for planar graphs
formal: Determine the asymptotic growth of \(\ell_{\mathrm{planar}}(n)\) up to universal constant factors, where \(\ell_{\mathrm{planar}}(n)\) is the least integer \(b\ge0\) permitting labels of \(b\) bits that determine every pairwise distance in every connected unweighted simple planar graph on \(n\ge2\) vertices using only the two labels.
why: Closing this polynomial gap would identify the information needed to distribute an entire planar graph metric into independent vertex labels.
status_note: Rechecked on 13 September 2026. The reviewed author and journal sources give the square-root upper bound and cube-root lower bound for exact unweighted planar distance labels. The faster-decoding variant uses larger labels. No constant-factor matching resolution of the unrestricted decoder model was located in the bounded later-work check; proofs were not independently audited.

progress.text: The improved scheme removes a logarithmic factor from the previous upper bound, leaving the exponent gap between \(n^{1/3}\) and \(n^{1/2}\).

definitions: For fixed \(n,b\), a permitted decoder is a function \(D:\{0,1\}^b\times\{0,1\}^b\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\). The same \(D\) must work for every connected unweighted simple undirected planar graph \(G\) with vertex set \([n]\): there must be a label assignment \(\lambda_G:[n]\to\{0,1\}^b\) such that \(D(\lambda_G(u),\lambda_G(v))=\operatorname{dist}_G(u,v)\) for all vertices, where distance counts edges on a shortest path. The decoder may depend on \(n\) and \(b\), but not on \(G\), and receives no shared graph data, vertex identifiers or additional input. Both the decoder domain and graph class are finite for fixed \(n,b\); no efficiency bound is imposed on constructing labels or decoding. The target measures label information alone, with arbitrary values on label pairs never used by an assignment. Known efficient schemes provide upper bounds in this unrestricted model as well. Here \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\); simple means no loops or parallel edges, and planar means admitting a drawing by nonintersecting arcs except at shared endpoints. Labels have the common fixed length \(b\); the target is the largest per-vertex bit length, not the sum over vertices. A finite admissible \(b\) always exists: each label can contain the whole finite graph description together with its vertex index, and a common decoder can recover graph distances from that description. Thus the least integer in the definition is well-defined.

context_blocks.text: A label is the information a vertex carries when the graph itself is unavailable. To answer a distance query, the decoder sees exactly the two endpoint labels. Its rule is common to the whole graph family, so it cannot have a different hidden graph stored for every labeling assignment.

Even the diagonal query constrains labels: a vertex is at distance zero from itself, while two distinct vertices in a connected unweighted graph are at positive distance. Two different vertices therefore cannot share a label. This simple observation only forces \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) bits, far below the known polynomial lower bound.

The reviewed upper bound is \(O(\sqrt n)\) bits per vertex, while the general lower bound is \(\Omega(n^{1/3})\). The gap is polynomial in \(n\), not just a missing logarithmic factor. An exact constant-factor answer must identify a rate that is both attainable and necessary for the same two-label model.

Decoding speed is a separate resource. The 2023 paper also gives a variant with polylogarithmic decoding time and \(O(\sqrt{n\log n})\)-bit labels. This card permits an arbitrary finite decoder for each \(n,b\), so a lower bound that applies only to fast decoders would not establish its information-theoretic optimum.

A shared distance oracle can distribute information between vertex identifiers and one common data structure; that common structure is absent here. Approximate distances, weighted graphs, and distances after a failure similarly change the information a pair of labels must provide. This target fixes connected, simple, unweighted planar graphs and exact edge counts.

The graph can determine its entire label assignment, but it cannot determine the decoder. The order of these choices permits graph-dependent labels while preventing the graph from being supplied for free through a query routine. No efficiency requirement is imposed on finding the labels or evaluating the decoder.

answer_criterion: Supply a specified asymptotic rate \(f(n)>0\) and a complete Lean-checked proof of constants \(c,C>0\), \(n_0\), such that \(cf(n)\le\ell_{\mathrm{planar}}(n)\le Cf(n)\) for all \(n\ge n_0\). Both bounds must use the same unrestricted exact-decoder model. Merely renaming the defining optimum, a one-sided improvement, or conditional hardness without its assumption proved does not meet this target. The accuracy requirement is constant-factor asymptotic matching, not an additive 0.01 error on big-O notation.
